name: Internet Domain Name System
description: A hierarchical distributed naming system in which domain names map to resource information via name servers and resolvers.

date.label: November 1983
date.basis: Date or interval stated or closely scoped by the cited source; see event caveats.

events.statement: RFC 882 described a distributed domain-name system and its facilities.
events.caveats: Publication describes a proposal and does not itself establish deployment.

evidence.supports: The original RFC sets out distributed domain names, resolvers and name servers.

date.label: around 1984
date.basis: Date or interval stated or closely scoped by the cited source; see event caveats.

events.statement: A later Internet growth report dates the introduction of DNS to around 1984 and describes a transition lasting almost four years.
events.caveats: This retrospective states approximate introduction and gradual transition but does not identify a specific first operational deployment or a universal adoption date.

evidence.supports: The RFC summarizes introduction and gradual deployment.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest cited dated event for this scoped record; a surviving witness or publication is not itself the invention date.

caveats: RFC 882 predates and was superseded by the 1987 DNS specifications; practical use developed gradually.

research.note: Second reader checked RFC 882 and RFC 1296: a dated specification and a later approximate introduction claim are distinct from a dated first operational installation.
